output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates were not caused by the agency operators or the printer firmware. The printer records show that from 4 Oct (22:10) PackBridge sent the printers a 36-month shelf life, so the expiry came out 12 months late. No operator overrides were made, and the printed text matched what was sent. Before that, 30 jobs were correct, including jobs after the firmware change and jobs run by agency operators.

The trigger was Regulatory Affairs' 3 Oct edit (CC-309). It entered 36 months for Veltranol, valid from 1 Mar 2027, and left 24 months as the current value. PackBridge sent the future value anyway, despite the vendor's claim that it can't. We haven't confirmed why. The camera only checks the print against the job, so it passed every carton.

The Line 1 day-shift lots, packed 21 and 29 Oct by permanent staff, are in the warehouse and need holding. Two other products (HX-15-30 and MR-05-14) have future-dated shelf-life edits and could be affected. I haven't checked whether they were.

Do not issue warnings or remove the agency operators. Do not switch off the camera check.

Next steps:
- Reset the Veltranol shelf-life records in the ERP.
- Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct.
- Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
- Inspect retained cartons of the other products with October shelf-life edits.
- Press Corvane to explain why PackBridge used a future-dated value.

I'm fairly confident in this.
